settings.heading: About Claire
settings.text:
Claire Cahill is a painter who works mostly in acrylic, with oils from time to time. For years her originals went straight from the easel to friends and people in her community.

Their encouragement is why this gallery exists. In her words, the support from people who loved her art inspired her to keep following it and see where it goes.

settings.caption: American Flag, acrylic paint skins in a 5×7 acrylic block
settings.heading: A flag for America’s 250th
settings.text:
For the nation’s 250th birthday Claire made an original flag from acrylic paint skins, layered into a high-texture surface. The original art is set inside a 5×7 acrylic block.

High-resolution prints of the flag are available too, for anyone who wants it on their wall.

settings.heading: Recognized by Tunnel to Towers
settings.text: The Tunnel to Towers Foundation reviewed Claire and her flag art and gave her a special designation as an official supporter.

settings.name: Acrylic paint skins
settings.text: Dried skins of acrylic paint, layered into a high-texture surface. This is how Claire made her flag for America’s 250th birthday.

settings.name: Palette knife and the chaos layer
settings.text: Paint applied with a palette knife, finished with a layer Claire calls the chaos layer. She uses this technique for the designs on her merchandise.

settings.name: Acrylic and oil
settings.text: Most of Claire’s paintings are acrylic, with oils from time to time.

settings.heading: See the work
settings.text: Originals, prints and keepsakes, gathered into rooms by theme.
